## TL;DR

Running board and pipeline cards no longer append noisy “active N ago” or inline elapsed time on healthy status lines; recency lives in the shared `data-tip` tooltip on hover, focus, long-press, and (for card recency hosts only) short tap. Silent and stuck tasks still show recency inline. Review pass 3’s global touch regression is fixed by scoping short-tap pinning to `data-tip-touch="tap"` and giving `pointercancel` its own handler.

## Work and rationale

Human feedback on #1057/#1055 showed running cards like “CODING · ACTIVE 1M AGO” wrapping to two lines without adding signal. The bundle item keeps the state label on the line and moves last-activity timing into the existing styled tooltip stack, which already serves hundreds of `data-tip` hosts across the app.

`card-activity-recency.ts` centralises popover copy (`agentLastActivityTip`, `stateElapsedTip`, `cardHintDataTip`). `retryHints.ts` and `TaskCard.vue` thread an optional `activityTip` through `CardHint`; healthy running labels omit inline activity while silent/stuck paths unchanged. `PipelineCard.vue` hides inline elapsed for non-stuck states and puts duration in the step tooltip.

Touch affordances landed in `lib/tooltip.ts` because the delegate hides on capture-phase `pointerdown`, which blocked any touch tooltip. Long-press and short-tap pinning were added so card hints could show recency without immediately opening the agent drawer or pipeline task. Pass 2 fixed click leakage with `preventDefault` on release and capture-phase click suppression.

Pass 3 correctly flagged that short-tap open + click suppression applied to every `data-tip` host, breaking SearchBar, NoticeBell, DoneErrorCard expand, and other real buttons. The fix keeps long-press on all hosts (discoverable hint without stealing primary actions) but limits short-tap open to elements with `data-tip-touch="tap"`. `TaskCard` and `PipelineCard` set that only when an `activityTip` / elapsed popover is present. `pointercancel` now clears the long-press timer only and does not run the release path that could pin a tooltip after a cancelled gesture.

## Approaches tried

Initial work reused hover/focus only; review 1 required touch. Global touch pinning in round 2 satisfied card tests but regressed unrelated controls in round 3. Opt-in `data-tip-touch` preserves card UX while restoring default button behaviour. An earlier attempt to fix handoff by editing `repoos.toml` and unrelated work files in the branch was reverted in favour of letting RepoOS own config drift at close-out.

## Challenges and blockers

Remote validation and UI smoke have timed out on prior handoffs; local scoped check and component tests are the reliable gate in this session. Coordinating with #1057’s card status rewrite required building on landed `CardHint` / evidence paths rather than duplicating label logic. Touch click arbitration is inherently global when one delegate serves every tooltip host—the opt-in attribute is the narrowest fix that does not fork tooltip implementations.

## Key learnings

Pushing interaction policy into a single global listener means every new gesture rule needs an explicit escape hatch for interactive hosts. Table-driven tests on `tooltip-touch.test.ts` plus mount tests on `TaskCard`/`PipelineCard` catch both the card requirement and the button regression class. For easter-egg UX bundles, one small module (`card-activity-recency.ts`) keeps TaskCard, pipeline, and retry hints aligned on copy format.
